title: Crowd control routing — sprint synthesis and ops notes
content:
Sprint period: 2029-08-27 -> 2029-09-03
Owners: Maya Chen (lead), Diego A. (kernel), Priya N. (kv/cache), Ethan P. (batching heuristics), Linh T. (oncall)

Purpose
- Capture what we tried this sprint for the "crowd-control" routing experiments (soft-eviction + routing by congestion tokens), summarize observed tradeoffs, and list next-step ops and PRs.

High-level summary (TL;DR)
- Traffic shaping via congestion-token routing + lightweight kernel fallback reduced high-p99 tail amplification during bursty multi-tenant spikes.
- Shadow runs show median latency +0.8% (within noise) and p99 reduced by ~12% under synthetic sawtooth traffic.
- CPU footprint for the new routing decision layer is small (~2% CPU on routing-control-plane); memory overhead from a transient token table is <15MB per zone.
- Two outstanding concerns: rare double-eviction race leading to transient 5xxs on warmup, and one workload saw increased cost due to extra inference fallbacks.

What we deployed this sprint
1) Routing: "congestion-token" prototype (diego/congestion-token-v1) deployed to canary (zone-us-west-2-a). Implementation: tokens accumulate per-client-window; when tokens exceed adaptive threshold we route new requests to lower-cost model variants or queue briefly.
2) Kernel fallback: added a non-blocking path to route to an alternative kernel compiled with simd-fallback (optimize-simd-accel-v2) when the primary kernel's queue depth exceeds a soft limit.
3) KV cache layering: shadow-written an "approx-lru" eviction agent that keeps a light-weight bloom-priority score to avoid thrashing for short-lived sessions.
4) Batching: heuristic "adaptive-window-mean-latency" updated to weight recent mean latency more heavily when tail noise > 7 sigma.

Key experiments & results
- Experiment A: synthetic sawtooth (burst 10x qps for 15s every 120s)
- Baseline (no crowd-control): p99 = 482ms
- With congestion-token + kernel fallback: p99 = 424ms (-12%)
- Median: baseline 86ms -> 87ms (+1.2%)
- Observations: queuing was smoother; fewer complete timeouts.
- Experiment B: multi-tenant blended traffic (10 tenants, skewed 80/20)
- One heavy tenant experienced ~6% higher token-related fallbacks causing additional cost; need tenant-level opt-out or cost-rebalancing accounting.
- Experiment C: shadow-KV layering on serving nodes
- Miss rate decreased 3.4% for sessionized workloads, but cold-start eviction events increased slightly during burst ramp.

Standup notes (daily micro-entries)
- 2029-08-28 (Diego): kernel handshake patch landed on staging; noticed scheduler jitter on amd64 nodes under contended loads. Next: reduce timer granularity.
- 2029-08-29 (Priya): KV shadow agent initial run (20% nodes) — good hit-rate improvement for chat-like workloads; edge-case: duplicate eviction when node restarts during compaction.
- 2029-08-30 (Ethan): Batching tweak pushed; observed minor improvement for 32-token requests but regressed for long contexts (>2048 tokens). Reverted for long contexts only.
- 2029-08-31 (Maya): Canary soak at us-west-2-a reached 48h; p95 stable, p99 improving, but rate-limiter interplay caused 503 spikes during traffic ramp. Need to adjust backpressure.
- 2029-09-02 (Linh): Oncall noticed 3x 5xx around 03:14 UTC; root cause was race in eviction+token-update causing token double-decrement. Hotfix PR attached.

Incidents and mitigations
- Incident: Double-eviction race (2029-09-02 03:14 UTC)
- Symptom: transient 500s for ~2 minutes in canary.
- Root cause: eviction async callback races with token reconciler; token table update undone leading to routing decisions that tried falling back to a kernel path that wasn't warmed.
- Mitigation applied: introduce per-client reconcile lock (fast-path, optimistic) + short TTL (5s) for reconciliation entries; hotfix PR merged to canary.
- Action: longer-term fix to rearchitect token updates to be idempotent (see action items).

Open technical questions
- How do we charge fallback-induced cost increases to tenants? Short-term: tag requests that hit fallback and include in billing metrics. Longer-term: expose per-tenant fallback budget and opt-out. (Priya + Finance follow-up).
- Is the per-client token table scalable past 200k active clients per zone? Need memory projection and potential sharding (Diego).
- Should we prefer queueing (short stall) over routing to lower-capacity models in certain latency-sensitive customers? Need product input and an A/B matrix.

Action items (owner - ETA)
- Make token updates idempotent and remove race window (Diego) - ETA: 2029-09-10
- Add per-request "fallback-tag" telemetry and wire into billing pipeline (Priya + Finance) - ETA: 2029-09-17
- Add tenant-level fallback opt-out switch in routing policy config (Maya + Product) - ETA: 2029-09-24
- Run memory projection + large-scale shard design doc (Diego + Ethan) - ETA: 2029-09-14
- Re-run long-context batching A/B with fallback disabled for >2048 token cases (Ethan) - ETA: 2029-09-09

Notes to self / TODO (informal)
- Remember to ping infra about ephemeral node restarts overlapping with compaction window (observed twice).
- Follow up with cost-ops about how the fallback charges show up in committed capacity vs. on-demand buckets.
- Add a short-run: test with fp16-only kernel fallback to see if cost/perf trade remains acceptable for low-priority tenants.

Meeting ask for next sync (2029-09-06)
- Diego: demo idempotent token update approach and show bench numbers.
- Priya: propose telemetry tag naming and plan to backfill historical data for charge estimates.
- Product: decide on tenant opt-out/auto-rebalance policy.

- Kernel patch: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5467 (optimize-simd-accel-v2)

End of notes.
